stem: Which of the following statements is correct about tympanometry?

options.text: It is a test of hearing
It is a test of the compliance of the tympanic membrane to different pressure changes
Middle ear effusion (i.e. “glue ear” or otitis media with effusion) leads to a flat Type B tympanogram
A normal tympanogram would be a Type C
Eustachian tube dysfunction presents as a Type A

explanation: Tympanometry assesses middle-ear system compliance (mobility) in response to changes in ear canal pressure. A flat Type B tympanogram is classically seen with middle ear effusion. Type A is normal, while Type C suggests negative middle-ear pressure often from Eustachian tube dysfunction.
rationale: Option C is the clearest single best answer. The item is preserved because it already contains one correct statement and distractors that are standard misconceptions.

optionExplanations.A: Tympanometry is not a hearing test; audiometry assesses hearing thresholds.
optionExplanations.B: This is essentially correct as tympanometry measures compliance of the tympanic membrane/middle ear system with pressure changes, but option C is the single best answer because it states a classic clinical correlation.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Middle ear effusion typically produces a flat Type B tympanogram.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect. A normal tympanogram is Type A, not Type C.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect. Eustachian tube dysfunction is usually associated with a Type C tympanogram due to negative middle-ear pressure.
